scope: First seven of the ordered fifteen uncertainties in company-eligibility-exclusions.json. No new discovery, production writes or removal authorisations.
criteria: Substantive continuing original technical development suffices, including shared, OSS-based and non-standalone technology. No patent, exclusivity, multi-customer or internal-only requirement. A company website claiming a platform exists does not by itself identify its developer.

results.reason: Current group AI Refinery engineering and platform development, plus a current Zurich application-development role, support retention as a technology developer with a local technical operation. Requiring the Zurich team to exclusively own a named global platform was too restrictive. This does not assert that AI Refinery is developed specifically in Zurich.

evidence.finding: Current official platform page attributes AI Refinery engineering to Accenture and lists 2026 platform activity.

Zurich application-development apprenticeship includes software/app design and maintenance; initial two years are with training partners, followed by Accenture projects. Evidence of local application development, not proof of local ownership of AI Refinery.

results.question: Does AutoMate itself continue to develop the insurance platform, including through an engineering partner, or only operate supplied software?
results.reason: Live broker/account/claims platform and white-label integrations are concrete, but the public material does not identify who builds or maintains the technology. The innovation claim is not enough to establish attribution; equally, there is no affirmative resale-only evidence. Retain without removal.

evidence.finding: Live platform describes broker sales, claims and quote functions, a Zurich office and ongoing solution creation. Does not identify development responsibility.
White-label offerings and calculator integration are explicit; extracted page retains translation templates. No developer attribution.
Public team roles mainly cover insurance, claims and operations; absence of a developer biography is not exclusion evidence.

results.reason: Current official WordPress offering explicitly lists custom-developed plugins used for tracking updates and maintenance. Together with detailed original ACF/Timber mapping, field caching and recursion-handling work, this supports continuing company-developed tooling, not merely installing WordPress. No separate marketed product or recent public commit is required.

evidence.finding: Current FAQ lists custom-developed plugins for tracking updates and maintenance; service description includes continuing development.
2018 technical account attributes automatic field mapping, caching and recursion handling to its own engineers; historical corroboration, not a fresh maintenance claim.

results.separateFollowup: Official pages disagree on Zurich address: WordPress page Selnaustrasse 3, older technical/headless pages Gasometerstrasse 9. Do not change a map address from this eligibility review.

results.question: Is a Forte technical operation still present at the listed Zurich site, despite the current official office roster omitting Switzerland?
results.reason: The named Migros employee-app project and current product-development roles support actual software development. No exclusivity or multiple-customer evidence is demanded. Swiss customers do not establish a Swiss office: the official account identifies the delivering Central Europe team with Berlin, and the current office list omits Zurich. Retain pending location clarification, not exclusion for consultancy branding.

evidence.finding: Official indexed July 2024 announcement identifies an employee app for Migros Aare; direct retrieval failed, primary indexed text was readable.
Official account identifies Berlin-based Central Europe delivery for Migros.
Current office roster lists Norway, Poland, Germany and Denmark, but not Zurich. Omission is a verification gap, not proof of closure.
Current Berlin product role supports continuing development, but not a Swiss development location.

results.question: Does icentic currently contribute technical development to beppo or another original platform, beyond its separately incorporated spin-off and client resource provision?
results.reason: Both sites explicitly connect beppo's origin to icentic, and current leadership overlaps. Beppo confirms continued Zurich platform development. Those facts do not establish current icentic participation after the spin-off; no exclusive ownership is required. Retain rather than infer service-only or transfer all beppo development to its originator.

evidence.finding: Current account describes incubation of digital spin-offs and shared founder/leadership with beppo.
Beppo identifies itself as an icentic spin-off and says its Zurich headquarters continues developing parking/fuel-theft tools.
Current catalogue includes turnkey software as well as staff/teams and development-centre setup; no named current icentic-owned platform branch.
Co-development and complete software work packages are substantive, but current contribution to the identified original platform remains unconfirmed.

results.question: Should the absorbed KOCH IT record become an Adnovum alias/site, and is its mapped Winterthur office still occupied?
results.reason: Technical development is not the unresolved issue. Adnovum explicitly reports Koch IT absorption in April 2026 and continued public-sector team operation. The independent company identity is outdated; the official current location list does not confirm Winterthur. Preserve records and relationships while main reviews successor representation; do not infer office closure or execute removal.

evidence.finding: 20 May 2026 announcement says the Koch IT absorption merger completed in April and incorporated its team into Adnovum public sector. Corrects earlier loose May-integration wording.
Current Swiss locations include Zurich, Bern and Lausanne; no Winterthur match.

results.reason: Official catalogue describes company-developed mechanical concepts, detailed construction, prototypes and small-series assemblies, including production and commissioning. Its homepage explicitly attributes assemblies to its own development. This is substantive original physical engineering, not merely generic advice or resale; demanding a separately named proprietary commercial product was too restrictive.

evidence.finding: Attributes prototypes/small-series assemblies to its own development and carries a Durot Electric reference for CAD, assembly and commissioning.
Full concept, design, prototype and small-series development workflow; current published Winterthur contact at Technoparkstrasse 2.

protected: Mecas, Reasoning Labs and all other records outside these first seven remain unchanged; sparse publicity is not treated as inactivity.
